s001: Give an abstract question a tangible subject.
s002: Person or object footage, key terms, a question, and the explanatory focus
s003: Psychology: seeing and understanding; history: people and their times; society: individuals and groups
s004: Establish the subject first, bring in the concept words from both sides, then reveal the question.
s006: Compare two easily confused concepts at a common scale.
s007: Two concepts, a shared subject, and an explanation of each
s008: Knowing / understanding; intention / outcome; policy / implementation
s009: Show both sides together, then emphasize each in turn. Do not use red crosses as a shortcut for right and wrong.
s011: Give a longer passage a clear route through the ideas.
s012: Two to five short headings, chapter footage, and the active item
s013: Observe / question / explain / reassess; origin / channel / node / impact
s014: Reveal tall, narrow media tabs in sequence. Use brightness and position to distinguish the active item.
s016: Ground a judgment in observable evidence and context.
s017: Source images, a detail to focus on, and two levels of explanation
s018: Pages and interpretation; archives and people; images and context
s019: Bring in the image, open the evidence panel, then shift attention from the material to its interpretation.
s021: Show who influences whom and how they are connected.
s022: People or entities, relationship labels, and direction
s023: Friends and choices; cities and trade; organizations and institutions
s024: Introduce the subjects, establish their relationships, then emphasize the key connection.
s026: Explain how a behavior reinforces itself.
s027: Three stages, a genuine feedback connection, and a way out
s028: Expectation / action / feedback; pressure / avoidance / greater difficulty starting
s029: Complete the connections in sequence, then hold the closed loop instead of rotating it continuously.
s031: Put a conspicuous result back in the context of the full sample.
s032: Total, selected count, units, and whether the data is factual or illustrative
s033: Three outcomes across ten attempts; proportions across different groups
s034: Establish the whole before highlighting a subset. Values must match the number of objects shown.
s036: Show the same subject changing over time.
s037: Three stages, a subject, a turning point, and actual years or stage names
s038: Before and after an event; the formation of a viewpoint; changes in an institution
s039: Move time consistently in one direction and leave enough reading time at turning points.
s041: First establish where the story takes place.
s042: Base map, extent, focus coordinates, place names, and historical period
s043: Cities, mountain passes, ports, and cultural regions
s044: Move from the region to the location, keeping camera movement and markers in the same coordinate system.
s046: Show direction of travel, stops, and sequence.
s047: Base map, route coordinates, stops, sequence, and an indication of whether the route is factual or schematic
s048: Migration, trade routes, diplomatic journeys, and the spread of knowledge
s049: Reveal the route in segments, introducing place names as it reaches them. Animation speed does not represent travel time.
s051: Compare spatial changes between two periods on the same base map.
s052: Dates for both periods, a shared projection, and boundary data and sources for each
s053: Territories, administrative areas, areas of control, and cultural diffusion
s054: Keep scale and viewing extent consistent. Alternate or juxtapose layers, and identify uncertain boundaries.
s056: Bring overlooked conditions into the explanation.
s057: A single source image or clip, a focal detail, the full view, and a change in judgment
s058: The context of a statement; the situation behind an expression; a detail in an artifact
s059: Start with the detail, then widen the view while keeping the original subject in the frame.
